characters.name: Gustave
characters.acts: Prologue and Act I (playable). He dies at the end of Act I.
characters.story_role: An engineer from Lumière and the lead protagonist of Act I. He is 32, so he is in the last year before his Gommage. His twin sister Emma is Lumière's Chief Councillor, and he and Emma are guardians of his foster sister Maelle. In the Prologue he says goodbye to Sophie when the number drops to 33. When Expedition 33 lands on the Continent, the white-haired man Renoir massacres most of the crew. Gustave regroups the survivors. At the end of Act I, Renoir ambushes the group on a beach and Gustave is killed protecting Maelle.
characters.combat_signature: Overcharge. His mechanical prosthetic arm, the Lumina Converter, builds charge as he fights. When fully charged it glows, and he can unleash Overcharge, a heavy lightning strike that breaks armor. On a charged Overcharge he says the expedition motto, 'For those who come after.'
characters.personal_goal: Reach and stop the Paintress before his own Gommage. Protect Maelle and leave something behind for those who come after.
characters.signature_objects: Mechanical prosthetic arm / Lumina Converter (Sandfall sold a life-size replica). The expedition motto 'For those who come after'. The expedition flag. His journal. The flower he takes to Sophie in the Prologue.
characters.tie_to_33: He embodies Expedition 33: one year left to live and doomed by the number 33. His death at the end of Act I is the game's big twist, and his motto is the theme of the whole expedition system.

characters.name: Lune
characters.acts: Act I to Act III (playable). She is gommaged by Renoir at the end of Act II and brought back by Maelle in Act III.
characters.story_role: The expedition's scholar, mage and pathfinder. She is entrusted with charting the route and carries heavy responsibility. Her parents were renowned researchers who died on an earlier expedition. They raised her to continue their work.
characters.combat_signature: Stains. Her skills generate elemental Stains (Fire, Ice, Lightning, Earth, Light), and other skills consume Stains for stronger effects. She is a caster, healer and status-effect support.
characters.personal_goal: Solve the mystery of the Paintress and finish her parents' work. Over the story she faces the grief and pressure her parents left her with.
characters.signature_objects: A dreamcatcher-like magic focus that holds her Stains. Her parents' research and journals. Sirène's Dress, the Act III area tied to her relationship level 6 quest, which gives 'Record: Lune'.
characters.tie_to_33: She is a core member of Expedition 33 and its knowledge-seeker. She wants to understand the Gommage rather than just survive it.

characters.name: Maelle / Alicia Dessendre
characters.acts: Prologue to Act III. She is the Act III protagonist, and Act III is titled 'Maelle'.
characters.story_role: A 16-year-old orphan who is Gustave's foster sister and Emma's ward. She feels she never belonged in Lumière and joins the expedition early to see the world. In Act III she recovers her memories. She is really Alicia Dessendre, the youngest daughter of the Painter family. Alicia was scarred in the fire that killed her brother Verso and left unable to speak. Within the Canvas, Aline repainted her as Maelle, born as a baby with no memory. Real-world Clea sent her into the Canvas to end the fight between Aline and Renoir. At the end of Act II, Renoir gommages Lumière, Maelle included, and she is thrown back into her real body. She returns as a Paintress, resurrects Lune and Sciel, and fights Renoir to save the Canvas. In the ending she and Verso fight over whether the Canvas should survive. Her ending is 'A Life to Paint'.
characters.combat_signature: Stances. She starts stanceless. Skills and weapon passives switch her between Offensive (+50% damage dealt and taken), Defensive (-50% damage taken, more AP from parries) and Virtuose (triple damage). Many skills gain bonuses when used from a specific stance. She fights with a rapier.
characters.personal_goal: Act I: find a place and family outside Lumière. Act III: keep the painted world and her friends alive, even against her own family.
characters.signature_objects: Rapier and fencing. Burn scars and the Alicia outfit, unlocked automatically in Act III. A brush (Paintress powers in Act III).
characters.tie_to_33: As a 16-year-old she is the youngest member of Expedition 33. Her secret identity connects Lumière to the Dessendre family behind the Gommage. In her ending she effectively becomes the new Paintress.

characters.name: Sciel
characters.acts: Prologue cameo, then Act I to Act III (playable). She is gommaged at the end of Act II and resurrected by Maelle in Act III.
characters.story_role: A warm, outgoing farmer-turned-teacher who smiles through tragedy. She worked on the Aquafarm project with Gustave and her best friend Sophie. Her husband Pierre died in an accident before his Gommage, and she also lost their unborn child. She is motivated to save Lumière's youth.
characters.combat_signature: Foretell and Twilight. Some skills apply Foretell stacks to enemies, and others consume them. Applying Foretell gives her a Sun charge and consuming it gives a Moon charge. With at least one of each at the start of her turn she enters Twilight for 2 turns, gaining +25% damage per charge consumed. Her weapon is a double-bladed scythe.
characters.personal_goal: Spare the children of Lumière the future she had, and come to terms with losing Pierre. In Act III she hopes to see him again.
characters.signature_objects: Double-bladed scythe (starting weapon Scieleson). Sun and Moon motifs. The farm and harvest theme (weapon 'Moisson' means harvest). Dorrie: Sciel is the one who finds Esquie's coral-breaking rock in Old Lumière.
characters.tie_to_33: She is a volunteer in her last year, a member of Expedition 33 and Sophie's best friend, who is gommaged in the Prologue.

characters.name: Monoco
characters.acts: Act II to Act III (playable). He is recruited at Monoco's Station.
characters.story_role: A Gestral and Verso's old friend, also friends with Esquie. He and Verso once lived together in Frozen Hearts and helped earlier expeditions. Monoco later stayed behind to guard the Grandis. To recruit him you must beat him in a duel and then defeat the Stalact boss at his mountain station. He is a battle-loving comic-relief character who collects the feet of defeated Nevrons. His questline is about rebirthing his protégé Noco at the Sacred River.
characters.combat_signature: Bestial Wheel and Nevron forms. He learns skills by defeating specific marked Nevrons and taking their feet, then transforms to use those Nevrons' moves. The Bestial Wheel rotates each turn through masks (Agile, Caster, Balanced, Heavy, Almighty). Using a skill that matches the current mask adds bonus effects.
characters.personal_goal: Fight strong opponents (he treats battle as meditation and thrill), protect his friends, and see Noco reborn.
characters.signature_objects: Collected Nevron feet. Masks on the Bestial Wheel. Monoco's Station. The Sacred River. The Thank You update's Baguette set (outfit, haircut and the Baguettaro weapon).
characters.tie_to_33: He joins Expedition 33's survivors with Verso. He is the Gestral (native Continent) view of the Paintress's world. He and Esquie rescue Alicia and Verso when Renoir starts destroying the Canvas.

characters.name: Verso
characters.acts: Act I as the mysterious man. Playable in Act II and Act III, which is titled 'Verso'. He is central to the ending and the Thank You update area Verso's Drafts.
characters.story_role: An immortal stranger who saves the survivors after Gustave dies. He is not the real Verso. He is a copy painted by Aline, and he knows he is painted. The real Verso Dessendre, Aline and Renoir's son, died in a fire set by the Writers while saving Alicia. The Canvas world was the real Verso's childhood painting and holds the last fragment of his soul. Painted Verso was in Expedition Zero with painted Renoir, Simon and Julie. His ending is 'A Life to Love', in which he ends the Canvas and sends Maelle home.
characters.combat_signature: Perfection ranks. A grade climbs D to C to B to A to S as he lands hits, dodges and parries, and drops when he takes damage. Higher rank means more damage. Many skills get extra effects at an exact rank, for example Perfect Break costs less AP at exactly rank B.
characters.personal_goal: Destroy the Paintress / Canvas to free his 'mother' and the real Verso's soul fragment, and finally find peace in death.
characters.signature_objects: Piano and music (the real Verso wanted to be a musician, not a painter). The letter from his sister Alicia. Esquie, his childhood creation. The Canvas itself. The Soarrie rock, which he gives to Esquie. Esquiso, the weapon from Osquio.
characters.tie_to_33: The world Expedition 33 lives in is literally his painting. He is the reason the Dessendres fight over the Canvas, and he is the person every Gommage is ultimately about.

characters.name: Esquie
characters.acts: Act I to Act III, plus the Thank You update. Recruited at Esquie's Nest in Act I.
characters.story_role: A huge, cheerful, balloon-like creature who becomes the party's world-map transport. Young Verso Dessendre painted him into his childhood Canvas, modelled on his favourite stuffed toy. He is an old friend of painted Verso and Monoco. He is friendly and endlessly patient, a 'French Winnie the Pooh', and his voice is full of 'whee/whoo' noises. He needs his lost magic rocks to gain traversal powers. Verso's Drafts contains a giant Esquie Head statue and Esquie's evil 'cousin' Osquio.
characters.combat_signature: Not a combat party member. His mechanics are world-map traversal unlocked by rocks: swim (Florrie), break coral (Dorrie), fly (Soarrie) and dive underwater (Urrie). In the original game he can also smash blue rock obstacles. His relationship levels unlock quests, and Urrie arrives at relationship level 6.
characters.personal_goal: Get his beloved rocks back (Florrie, Dorrie, Urrie, Soarrie), have fun and help his friends. He 'can be sad or bad or even rad, but never ever ever mad.'
characters.signature_objects: Four magic rocks (Florrie, Dorrie, Urrie, Soarrie). Esquie's Nest. His grumpy turtle neighbour François. The Esquie Head statue and Esquie outfits from the update. Osquio, his rival cousin.
characters.tie_to_33: Without him the expedition cannot cross the Continent's sea or reach the Monolith. He flies the party up against the titanic Paintress at the end of Act II. He is a piece of young Verso's soul and imagination, the origin of the whole Canvas.

characters.name: The Paintress / Aline Dessendre
characters.acts: Paints 33 in the Prologue. Final boss of Act II at the Monolith. Real-world scenes in Act III and the endings.
characters.story_role: The mother of Verso, Clea and Alicia, wife of Renoir, and described as head of the Painters' Council. Grieving the real Verso, she entered his Canvas and refused to leave. She painted copies of her family (Verso, Renoir, Clea, and Alicia/Maelle) to live with. Her fight with Renoir caused the Fracture, which split Lumière from the Continent and created the Monolith. She ended up trapped at the top of the Monolith. Each year 'the Paintress' paints a decreasing number on the Monolith, and everyone of that age or older in Lumière is gommaged into petals. Late-game sources say the erasing is Renoir's power and the number is Aline's warning or countdown. Expedition 33 defeats her at the end of Act II, sending Aline back to the real world.
characters.combat_signature: A boss, not playable. Act II climax at the Monolith, including a titanic Paintress form fought after Esquie flies the party up. For a Root design, her theme is painting, creating and spawning: she paints numbers and creatures into the world.
characters.personal_goal: Stay inside her dead son's painting with her painted family and keep the Canvas alive against Renoir. This is grief as refusal.
characters.signature_objects: The Monolith and the number painted on it (33 at game start). Paint and brush. Red petals of the Gommage. The Paintress's Heart in Old Lumière (destroyed in Act II).
characters.tie_to_33: She is the reason for the number 33 and for every Expedition. The game is named after her countdown, and Expedition 33 exists to kill her. Thematically she is the 'mother who has been playing too many board games' with her children's world.

characters.name: Renoir (painted, the 'white-haired man')
characters.acts: Act I and Act II. He is destroyed at the Monolith at the end of Act II.
characters.story_role: The main visible antagonist of Acts I and II. He is a copy of Aline's husband that she painted. With dark Nevrons (some sources call them 'Noirs') he slaughters Expedition 33 on the beach when they arrive. He kills Gustave at the end of Act I. The party fights him in Old Lumière and again with the 'Dark Creature' near the end of the Monolith. With the Curator's help, Maelle erases him.
characters.combat_signature: A boss, not playable. Recurring Act II fights in Old Lumière and the Monolith. In Act I he is effectively unbeatable.
characters.personal_goal: Protect the Paintress / Aline and stop the expeditions from reaching her.
characters.signature_objects: White hair and an aristocratic painter look. Dark Nevron minions. The beach ambush. Expedition Zero, which he led with painted Verso.
characters.tie_to_33: He is the reason Expedition 33 nearly dies on day one, and the reason past expeditions vanished.

characters.name: The Curator / Renoir Dessendre (real)
characters.acts: At camp from Act I. Revealed in Act III. Final boss of Act III in Lumière.
characters.story_role: The real Renoir, father of Verso, Clea and Alicia. He entered the Canvas to drag Aline and later Alicia out, because Painters who stay in a Canvas too long die. After the Fracture, Aline imprisoned him beneath the Monolith. He slipped out in a faceless, ethereal form, the Curator, and quietly helped Expedition 33 defeat the Paintress so Aline would be expelled. Sources state that the real Renoir's power erases the oldest of Aline's creations, which is the Gommage. Once Aline is out, he gommages Lumière and tries to destroy the Canvas. He is the final boss.
characters.combat_signature: As the Curator he is the camp NPC who upgrades weapons with Chroma Catalysts. As the final-boss Renoir he has a completely different moveset from the painted Renoir fights.
characters.personal_goal: End the Canvas so his wife and daughter grieve properly and survive.
characters.signature_objects: Faceless Curator form and the camp. Chroma Catalysts and weapon upgrades. The prison under the Monolith. Renoir's Drafts (late-game area). His theme 'Une vie à t'aimer'.
characters.tie_to_33: He is the hidden hand behind the Gommage and the true final opponent. He is also the man who quietly helped Expedition 33 succeed.

characters.name: Clea Dessendre (real) and painted Clea
characters.acts: The real Clea appears in lore and Act III. Painted Clea is an Act III superboss in the Flying Manor. 'Clea Unleashed' was added to the Endless Tower in the Thank You update.
characters.story_role: The real Clea is the eldest Dessendre daughter and a Painter. She is fighting a war outside the Canvas against the Writers who set the fire. She wants the Canvas destroyed and sent Alicia in to end her parents' conflict. She secretly abducted and repainted the painted Clea (Aline's copy) to keep producing Nevrons. This drains Aline's chroma so Renoir can erase the world. Painted Clea, the 'Regent' in the Flying Manor, is the source of the Nevrons. She is a secret superboss, recommended level 80+.
characters.combat_signature: A boss, not playable. The Flying Manor superboss is surrounded by Nevron creations. Clea Unleashed is a harder version in the Endless Tower.
characters.personal_goal: Real Clea: break the family's grief cycle and win the war against the Writers. Painted Clea: endlessly create 'perfect' Nevrons.
characters.signature_objects: Flying Manor. Nevrons. Clea Haircut and Clea Music Record (Endless Tower rewards). Her letters and orders.
characters.tie_to_33: She is the reason the Continent is full of the Nevrons that kill expeditions. She engineers the conditions for the Gommage to keep spreading, and she sends Alicia in.

characters.name: Sophie
characters.acts: Prologue
characters.story_role: Gustave's ex-girlfriend and Sciel's best friend, who worked on the Aquafarm with them. She is 33 when the number drops, and is gommaged in the Prologue after Gustave says goodbye.
characters.combat_signature: None (non-combat NPC).
characters.personal_goal: To face the Gommage with dignity and say goodbye.
characters.signature_objects: The flower Gustave brings her. The Gommage ceremony in Lumière. Red petals.
characters.tie_to_33: She is the first face of the number 33: the opening scene shows the cost of the Gommage through her.

characters.name: Emma
characters.acts: Prologue (Lumière)
characters.story_role: Gustave's twin sister and Lumière's Chief Councillor. She and Gustave are Maelle's guardians. She formally sends off Expedition 33 and oversees expedition logistics. She dislikes the expeditions, especially Gustave joining, but accepts that they matter.
characters.combat_signature: None (non-combat NPC).
characters.personal_goal: Keep Lumière running and her family safe.
characters.signature_objects: The Lumière council and the expedition send-off ceremony.
characters.tie_to_33: She is the institution that launches Expedition 33.

characters.name: Simon
characters.acts: Act III optional (The Abyss, inside Renoir's Drafts). 'Simon the Divergent Star' was added to the Endless Tower in the Thank You update.
characters.story_role: A member of Expedition Zero, painted Verso's close friend and painted Clea's love interest. He was believed dead but was sealed in the Abyss. He had meant to fight the Curator to free Clea. The real Clea repainted him as her enforcer, and his mind is broken.
characters.combat_signature: The hardest superboss, with a roughly 50 million HP pool. His later phases use 'We Lost', a remix of Renoir's theme.
characters.personal_goal: Free Clea from her suffering, now twisted into obeying her.
characters.signature_objects: The Abyss, Renoir's Drafts, and the Simon haircuts added in the update.
characters.tie_to_33: He is a ghost of Expedition Zero, the first expedition after the Fracture. He shows what became of the earliest attempt that came before Expedition 33.

characters.name: Julie (Expedition Zero)
characters.acts: Lore / flashbacks (appears in Maelle's nightmares)
characters.story_role: A deceased member of Expedition Zero ('Search and Rescue'). She grew suspicious of Verso's immortality and had him kidnapped. Painted Renoir convinced Verso she was Clea's creation and ordered her death, and Verso killed her.
characters.combat_signature: None known.
characters.personal_goal: Find survivors after the Fracture and expose what she thought was a traitor.
characters.signature_objects: Expedition Zero, and the Forgotten Battlefield area where the betrayal happened.
characters.tie_to_33: She is part of the expedition tradition's dark origin, the first in a line that ends with 33.

characters.name: Golgra
characters.acts: Act I (Gestral Village) and later fights through Monoco's quest (Sacred River, Dark Gestral Arena)
characters.story_role: The female chief of the Gestral Village. She runs the village's fighting culture, and you must win the Gestral Village tournament to get the password through the eastern gate to Esquie's Nest. She is an optional duel boss with very high HP (about 3.4M) and is fought several times through Monoco's quest.
characters.combat_signature: A boss: pure physical damage using her flexible body.
characters.personal_goal: Lead and test the Gestrals through combat.
characters.signature_objects: Gestral Village and its tournament / arena. Dark Gestral Arena.
characters.tie_to_33: She is the gatekeeper on Expedition 33's route to Esquie in Act I.

characters.name: François
characters.acts: Act I and Act III (Esquie's Nest)
characters.story_role: Esquie's grumpy turtle neighbour. Esquie claims François stole his rock Florrie, and the party beats him to recover it. In Act III, at Esquie's relationship level 5, he holds Urrie and refuses to trade, which leads to a rematch.
characters.combat_signature: A boss, weak to Dark damage.
characters.personal_goal: Keep the rocks and be left alone (comic rival).
characters.signature_objects: Florrie and Urrie, and Esquie's Nest.
characters.tie_to_33: He blocks Expedition 33's ability to cross the sea (Florrie) and later to dive (Urrie).

characters.name: Osquio
characters.acts: Thank You update (Verso's Drafts, Root of All Evil); Act III and post-game
characters.story_role: Esquie's self-proclaimed 'evil cousin' and arch-enemy. Young Verso created him to embody his negative thoughts, as the villain of his childhood Canvas. He taunts Verso that he will always be a painter and never a musician. He is the final boss of Verso's Drafts.
characters.combat_signature: A boss with unusual attacks and endgame-level stats (comparable to Simon). Defeating him rewards Esquiso (a Verso weapon) and the Osquio outfit and haircut.
characters.personal_goal: Play the villain to Esquie and Verso's hero.
characters.signature_objects: Root of All Evil, reached by a train by the giant Esquie Head statue. Osquio outfits.
characters.tie_to_33: He is the dark mirror of Esquie and a look at young Verso, the child whose Canvas Expedition 33 lives in.

characters.name: The Mimes
characters.acts: All acts. The first is in the Prologue in Lumière (the 'A Peculiar Encounter' trophy). A new Mime was added in Verso's Drafts.
characters.story_role: A recurring sight gag: silent black-and-white French mimes hidden in nearly every major area, about 17 across 12 locations. They are optional mini-bosses.
characters.combat_signature: An optional mini-boss. Whoever lands the killing blow earns a haircut, often with a matching outfit.
characters.personal_goal: None stated. Pure absurdist comedy.
characters.signature_objects: Haircuts and outfits, and the Baguette set for Monoco from the update's Mime.
characters.tie_to_33: They are 'the one constant' Expedition 33 meets across the Continent, the game's running joke.

characters.name: Noco
characters.acts: Act II and Act III (Monoco's questline)
characters.story_role: An ambitious Gestral merchant and Monoco's protégé. Monoco's final quest is about bringing Noco back to life at the Sacred River, where dead Gestrals are reborn with most of their memories gone.
characters.combat_signature: None (merchant).
characters.personal_goal: Prove his ambition as a merchant.
characters.signature_objects: His shop and the Sacred River.
characters.tie_to_33: A minor character who adds to Monoco's story and Gestral lore.

esquie_lost_items.name: Florrie
esquie_lost_items.power_it_restores: Swim. Esquie can carry the party across the sea to new coasts and islands.
esquie_lost_items.who_holds_it_and_where: François, Esquie's grumpy turtle neighbour, at Esquie's Nest (Act I). Esquie says François stole it, and the party beats François in a boss fight to recover it. The swimming then takes them on to Stone Wave Cliffs, the last Act I area.

esquie_lost_items.name: Dorrie
esquie_lost_items.power_it_restores: Break coral. Esquie can smash coral reefs that block sea routes.
esquie_lost_items.who_holds_it_and_where: No rival holds it. Sciel finds it in Old Lumière, the sunken old city (Act II), while the party goes to destroy the Paintress's Heart.

esquie_lost_items.name: Soarrie
esquie_lost_items.power_it_restores: Fly. Esquie can fly with the party on his back, reaching the Monolith's top and most of the Act III map, including the Endless Tower, Sky Island and Flying Manor.
esquie_lost_items.who_holds_it_and_where: Verso. He reveals he had already recovered it at the top of the Monolith, when Aline unleashes the titanic Paintress at the end of Act II, and Esquie flies the party into that fight. Sources do not say who had it before Verso or where he found it.

esquie_lost_items.name: Urrie
esquie_lost_items.power_it_restores: Underwater diving. Esquie can dive at glowing blue whirlpools in the ocean, which give rewards and open hidden areas, including access to Renoir's Drafts and the Abyss.
esquie_lost_items.who_holds_it_and_where: François again, at Esquie's Nest. At Esquie's relationship level 5 (after Act II), Esquie talks about his long-missing favourite rock Urrie and points the party to François. François refuses to trade, the party defeats him in a rematch, and returning Urrie raises Esquie to level 6.

continent_locations.name: Lumière
continent_locations.note: An island city based on Paris, with a twisted Eiffel Tower and a broken Arc de Triomphe. The Fracture split it from the Continent. The Gommage ceremony and Expedition send-off happen here. The final boss (real Renoir) is fought here in Act III. Natural 'home' clearing for the player.

continent_locations.name: The Monolith
continent_locations.act: Visible from the Prologue; Act II finale
continent_locations.note: A giant stone spire across the sea where the Paintress paints the yearly number. A barrier protects it until the two Axons are defeated. Areas include 'The Monolith' and 'Inside The Monolith'. Renoir and the Dark Creature are fought here, then the Paintress. Aline was trapped at the top and the real Renoir underneath.

continent_locations.name: Spring Meadows
continent_locations.note: The first area after landing. Boss: Eveque.

continent_locations.name: Flying Waters
continent_locations.note: Boss: Goblu.

continent_locations.name: Ancient Sanctuary
continent_locations.note: Boss: Ultimate Sakapatate, a Gestral-made machine.

continent_locations.name: Gestral Village
continent_locations.note: Chief Golgra and the tournament. Winning it gives the password to the eastern gate toward Esquie's Nest.

continent_locations.name: Esquie's Nest
continent_locations.note: Esquie's home, where François holds Florrie and later Urrie.

continent_locations.name: Stone Wave Cliffs
continent_locations.note: The last Act I area, reached by swimming. Lampmaster boss, and the mysterious man (Verso) appears. Gustave dies at the end of Act I, when painted Renoir ambushes the group on a beach.

continent_locations.name: Forgotten Battlefield
continent_locations.note: Boss: Dualliste. Linked to Expedition Zero's betrayal of Verso by Julie's team.

continent_locations.name: Monoco's Station
continent_locations.note: A mountain station. Duel Monoco, then fight the Stalact boss to recruit him.

continent_locations.name: Old Lumière
continent_locations.note: The drowned old city. Destroy the Paintress's Heart, fight painted Renoir, and Sciel finds Esquie's rock Dorrie here.

continent_locations.name: Visages
continent_locations.note: Axon modelled on Verso. Bosses Visages and Mask Keeper, with sub-vales.

continent_locations.name: Sirène
continent_locations.note: Axon modelled on Aline. Glissando guards the approach near the Crumbling Path.

continent_locations.name: Gestral Beach(es) / Sacred River
continent_locations.note: Gestral side areas. The Sacred River is a river of chroma where dead Gestrals are reborn, used in Monoco's quest.

continent_locations.name: Frozen Hearts
continent_locations.note: A snowy area where Verso and Monoco once lived.

continent_locations.name: Yellow Harvest / Falling Leaves / Crimson Forest / Red Woods / Lost Woods
continent_locations.note: Optional regions that suit Root's forest clearings. Crimson Forest is near the Endless Tower.

continent_locations.name: Endless Tower
continent_locations.note: In the southwest of the map, south of the Crimson Forest. A gauntlet of 11 stages with 3 trials each, 33 trials in total. The Thank You update added the 'Clea Unleashed' and 'Simon the Divergent Star' bosses. A natural landmark.

continent_locations.name: Flying Manor
continent_locations.note: A floating manor inside a ring of floating rocks above the southwest of the big snowy island. Lair of painted Clea, the Nevron-maker superboss.

continent_locations.name: Renoir's Drafts / The Abyss
continent_locations.note: The highest-level area, reached by diving with Urrie. Simon waits in the Abyss past the Golden Tree rest point.

continent_locations.name: Sky Island
continent_locations.note: A small floating island east of the central snowy island, with a Chromatic boss.

continent_locations.name: Sirène's Dress
continent_locations.note: Reached by flight from behind Sirène. Lune's level 6 relationship area.

continent_locations.name: The Reacher
continent_locations.note: An Axon area modelled on Alicia, on the northwest shoreline near Visages. A fourth Axon, The Hauler, is modelled on Clea.

continent_locations.name: Flying Casino / White Sands / Floating Cemetery / Endless Night Sanctuary / Sunless Cliffs / Isle of the Eyes / The Canvas / Dark Gestral Arena / Esoteric Ruins / Twilight Quarry / The Manor / Painting Workshop
continent_locations.note: Extra side areas to fill out a 12-clearing map or to use as ruins and landmarks.

continent_locations.name: Verso's Drafts
continent_locations.act: Act III (Thank You update, v1.5.0, Dec 2025)
continent_locations.note: A storybook world from young Verso's imagination, reached through a portal next to or east of Lumière. Sub-areas: Candy Land, Reverie Path, Treehouse Forest, Licornapieds Station, and Root of All Evil (Osquio's lair, reached by a train at the giant Esquie Head statue). A natural landmark or hireling theme.

enemies_and_factions.name: Nevrons
enemies_and_factions.note: The general hostile creatures, which appeared after the Fracture and change with each area's theme or emotion. Lore says painted Clea makes them (repainted by the real Clea) to drain Aline's chroma.

enemies_and_factions.name: Axons
enemies_and_factions.note: Four giant Nevrons with hearts of pure chroma, said to be made by Renoir in the image of Dessendre family members: Visages and the Mask Keeper (Verso), Sirène (Aline), The Reacher (Alicia) and The Hauler (Clea). In Act II the party defeats Visages and Sirène to forge a weapon that can pierce the Monolith barrier.

enemies_and_factions.name: Chromatic Nevrons
enemies_and_factions.note: Optional elite boss variants, for example Chromatic Abbest, Chromatic Lancelier, Chromatic Portier, Chromatic Ranger Sakapatate and Chromatic Clair / Obscur. Good 'elite spawn' or loot-carrier theme.

enemies_and_factions.name: Mimes
enemies_and_factions.note: A recurring comic optional mini-boss in almost every region (about 17). They drop haircuts and outfits.

enemies_and_factions.name: Petanks
enemies_and_factions.note: Iron-ball Nevrons with legs that run away. You chase them until they stop on glowing stones, then fight them for rich loot. A good model for 'enemies that spawn carrying an item you must catch'.

enemies_and_factions.name: White Nevrons
enemies_and_factions.note: Colourless Nevrons that can talk and are not hostile. They give side quests (e.g. Blanche, and the Small Bourgeon area).

enemies_and_factions.name: Gestrals
enemies_and_factions.note: A friendly but fight-loving native people. Chief Golgra; Monoco and Noco are Gestrals. Young Gestrals are 'patates', and dead Gestrals are reborn at the Sacred River with most memories lost. They build machines called Sakapatates (Ultimate Sakapatate is an Act I boss). Areas include Gestral Village, Gestral Beaches, Dark Gestral Arena and an Ancient Gestral City.

enemies_and_factions.name: Grandis
enemies_and_factions.note: A people Monoco stayed behind to guard. Minor faction.

enemies_and_factions.name: Renoir's dark Nevrons ('Noirs')
enemies_and_factions.note: The dark creatures that massacre Expedition 33 on the beach with painted Renoir. The exact in-game name is unconfirmed.

enemies_and_factions.name: Expeditions of Lumière (Expedition Zero to 33)
enemies_and_factions.note: One expedition sails every year after the Gommage. Expedition Zero (Search and Rescue) included painted Verso, painted Renoir, Simon and Julie. The journals of past expeditions are collectibles. The motto is 'For those who come after.'

enemies_and_factions.name: The Dessendre family / Painters
enemies_and_factions.note: Real-world Painters who can enter Canvases: Renoir, Aline (head of the Painters' Council), Clea, Verso (died) and Alicia.

enemies_and_factions.name: The Writers
enemies_and_factions.note: A rival real-world group of artists at war with the Dessendres. Their arson caused the fire that killed Verso and scarred Alicia. They are not on the Continent.

enemies_and_factions.name: Main story bosses
enemies_and_factions.note: Eveque (Spring Meadows), Goblu (Flying Waters), Ultimate Sakapatate (Ancient Sanctuary), François (Esquie's Nest), Lampmaster (Act I), Dualliste (Forgotten Battlefield), Stalact (Monoco's Station), Renoir (Old Lumière), Visages and Mask Keeper, Glissando, Sirène, Renoir and the Dark Creature (Monolith), The Paintress, Creation, and Renoir as the final boss (Act III).

enemies_and_factions.name: Superbosses
enemies_and_factions.note: Painted Clea (Flying Manor), Simon (The Abyss), Golgra (repeat duels) and the Endless Tower gauntlet.

enemies_and_factions.name: Verso's Drafts enemies (Thank You update)
enemies_and_factions.note: Osquio (final boss); Chromatic bosses Barbasucette (summons sweets that buff allies), Franctale, Licorne and Machinapieds; optional Licornapieds and the Half-baked Gestral; and a new Mime.

dlc_update_content: E33's 'Thank You' Update (v1.5.0) is free. It was announced at The Game Awards 2025 (where E33 won Game of the Year) and released on Dec 11–12, 2025 for PS5, Xbox and PC.

Verso's Drafts is a new storybook region tied to young Verso, reached from Act III through a portal near or east of Lumière. Sub-areas: Candy Land, Reverie Path, Treehouse Forest, Licornapieds Station and Root of All Evil.

New bosses: Osquio (final boss, rewards the Esquiso weapon for Verso and the Osquio set); 4 new Chromatic bosses (Barbasucette, Franctale, Licorne, Machinapieds); optional Licornapieds and the Half-baked Gestral; and a new Mime that gives Monoco's Baguette set and the Baguettaro weapon.
New Endless Tower bosses: 'Clea Unleashed' and 'Simon the Divergent Star', both variations of main-game bosses.

About 20 new outfits (77 base plus 20 new): Chic and Esquie outfits for most characters, Osquio outfits for Lune, Maelle, Sciel and Verso, a Visages outfit for Verso, a Baguette outfit for Monoco, and Simon, Esquie and Osquio haircuts.
Also new weapons, Luminas, Pictos, quests, music tracks, Photo Mode, loadouts, 7 new languages (19 total), and Steam Deck and ROG Xbox Ally 'Verified' status.

Separate from E33, for the Root side: Root digital's 'Hirelings & Landmarks' DLC was released on Oct 20, 2025 ($9.99). It adds hirelings (e.g. Forest Patrol, Rabbit Scouts, Corvid Spies) and landmarks. Three hirelings join any game where they are enabled, each in a promoted or demoted form.
uncertainties: WebFetch was blocked for every wiki and news domain I tried (fandom, wiki.gg, fextralife, gamefaqs, maxroll, wikipedia, pcgamesn, xbox wire and others). Every fact here comes from web-search result snippets, so wording should be spot-checked in game or on a wiki before final copy.
The user's 'nuts': Esquie's lost items are magic ROCKS / stones named Florrie, Dorrie, Urrie and Soarrie. Nothing in the game is called 'nuts'.

Who held Soarrie before Verso is not established. Sources only say Verso had already recovered it and reveals this at the top of the Monolith (end of Act II). One source says flying unlocks 'at the start of Act III'.
Dorrie is found by Sciel in Old Lumière, not taken from a rival, according to one fandom snippet plus guides saying coral-breaking unlocks after Old Lumière. Medium confidence.
Urrie: sources disagree on whether the hint comes at relationship level 5 or 6. They agree that you beat François again at Esquie's Nest and that returning it gives level 6 / diving.
Florrie: Esquie 'supposedly' says François stole it. It may be a comic misunderstanding rather than a real theft.

Gommage mechanics: early or marketing framing says the Paintress causes it. Late-game sources say the real Renoir's power does the erasing and Aline's number is a warning or countdown. Treat it as 'the Paintress paints the number; Renoir is behind the erasing' and avoid over-specifying.

There are two Renoirs. The painted Renoir (white-haired old man) is the Act I–II antagonist, kills Gustave and is erased at the Monolith. The real Renoir is the Curator and the Act III final boss. Some summaries mix them up.
There are two Cleas. The real Clea (eldest daughter, war with the Writers, sends Alicia in) and the painted Clea (repainted by the real Clea, makes Nevrons, Flying Manor superboss).

Gustave's exact death location: sources agree it is the end of Act I, on a beach ambush by painted Renoir after the Act I areas. Stone Wave Cliffs is the last listed Act I area, but the precise map spot is not confirmed.
Lune's parents' expedition number was given once as 'Expedition 46'. It is unverified and omitted above.
The beach massacre minions are called 'Noirs' / 'Noir Nevrons' by one source only. The landing beach may be the 'Dark Shores' area (unconfirmed).
Verso's Drafts placement is described both as 'next to / east of Lumière' and 'in the southern Continent'.
The 'Creation' boss's exact area and the 'Painted Love' fight (one source says the Curator and the Paintress together) are unverified and left out of detail.

Root Homeland expansion: the physical edition lists Q3 2026 and adds the Lilypad Diaspora, Twilight Council and Knaves of the Deepwood. I found no confirmed Root digital release, so assume it is unavailable for the mod.
Voice-actor names surfaced in searches but are deliberately not used. Barks must be original writing and not imitate any actor.

factions.name: Marquise de Cat
factions.engine: Pieces: 25 cat warriors, 6 sawmills, 6 workshops, 6 recruiters, 8 wood tokens, 1 keep token. Setup: the keep goes in a corner clearing, with 1 warrior in every clearing except the one diagonally opposite. One sawmill, one workshop and one recruiter start in or next to the keep, and 5 of each building stay on the faction-board tracks. Birdsong: place 1 wood at each sawmill. Daylight: craft using workshops, then up to 3 actions: Battle, March (2 moves), Recruit (1 warrior at each recruiter, once per turn), Build (pay wood from connected clearings she rules; the cost rises as each track empties) and Overwork (spend a card that matches a sawmill clearing to add wood). Each bird card spent buys one extra action. Evening: draw 1 card, plus bonus draws uncovered on the recruiter track. Keep: only the Marquise can place pieces in the keep clearing. Field Hospitals: when her warriors are removed, she may spend a card that matches their clearing to return them to the keep.
factions.how_it_scores: Scores VP each time she builds. The VP printed under the slot uncovered on that building's track rises as more of that type are built. She also scores normally for crafting item cards and for removing enemy buildings and tokens (1 VP each, a universal rule).
factions.board_state_it_creates: Number and position of sawmills, workshops and recruiters; wood tokens per clearing; keep token location (a corner clearing); cat warriors in every clearing; which clearings she rules (most warriors plus buildings). These make a good 'industry or occupation' check, e.g. 'have X buildings in clearings of every suit'.
factions.digital_bot_available: Yes. The built-in Dire Wolf AI plays it, and the Clockwork 'Mechanical Marquise 2.0' bot comes in the Clockwork Expansion DLC.

factions.name: Eyrie Dynasties
factions.engine: Pieces: 20 bird warriors, 7 roosts, 4 leader cards (Builder, Charismatic, Commander, Despot), 2 Loyal Vizier cards. The Decree has 4 columns: Recruit, Move, Battle, Build. Birdsong: add 1-2 cards to the Decree (at most one bird), and place a new roost if none is on the map. Daylight: craft with roosts, then resolve every Decree card left to right; each action must happen in a clearing that matches the card's suit (birds are wild). If any card cannot be resolved, Turmoil follows: lose VP equal to the bird cards in the Decree, discard the Decree except the viziers, depose the leader, choose a new one, and Daylight ends. Lords of the Forest: the Eyrie rule clearings they tie for. Disdain for Trade: crafted items give only 1 VP.
factions.how_it_scores: Each Evening, scores VP from the roost track by how many roosts are on the map (from memory roughly 0,1,2,3,4,4,5; not verified). Also scores by removing enemy buildings and tokens. Turmoil costs VP.
factions.board_state_it_creates: Roost count and positions, warriors per clearing, Decree length and current leader (card state), clearings ruled, including tied ones. Natural 'spread across N clearings' and 'hold corners' checks.
factions.digital_bot_available: Yes. The built-in AI plays it, and the Clockwork 'Electric Eyrie' bot comes in the Clockwork Expansion DLC.

factions.name: Woodland Alliance
factions.engine: Pieces: 10 warriors, 3 bases (fox, rabbit, mouse), 10 sympathy tokens. A Supporters stack of cards is capped at 5 while no base is on the map. Birdsong: Revolt (spend 2 supporters that match a sympathetic clearing: remove all enemy pieces there, place the matching base and warriors, gain an officer) and Spread Sympathy (spend supporters that match the target clearing; the cost rises as the track fills, plus extra under Martial Law). Daylight: craft using sympathy, Mobilize (a card goes to supporters), Train (spend a card that matches a base to gain an officer). Evening: Military Operations, one per officer: Move, Battle, Recruit at a base, Organize (remove a warrior to place sympathy). Outrage: anyone who removes sympathy or moves into a sympathetic clearing must give the Alliance a matching card. Guerrilla War: as defender, the Alliance uses the higher die. Losing a base discards that suit's supporters and half the officers.
factions.how_it_scores: Scores the VP printed on the sympathy track each time a sympathy token is placed (more tokens on the map means bigger payouts). It also scores for crafting and for removing enemy buildings and tokens, including through revolts.
factions.board_state_it_creates: Sympathy tokens per clearing (count and suits), bases on the map, officers, warriors. Ideal for 'win the hearts of N clearings' or 'revolt in every suit' checks.
factions.digital_bot_available: Yes. The built-in AI plays it, and the Clockwork 'Automated Alliance' bot comes in the Clockwork Expansion DLC.

factions.name: Vagabond
factions.expansion: Base game (Thief, Tinker, Ranger). The Riverfolk DLC adds 3 characters and support for a second Vagabond; Exiles & Partisans & Vagabonds adds 3 more.
factions.engine: One pawn, which is not a warrior and cannot rule. Items sit on the character card and are exhausted or damaged as they are used. A relationship track for each non-Vagabond faction runs Indifferent, Amiable, Friendly, Allied, or the faction becomes Hostile. Quest cards are kept face up. Birdsong: refresh 3 items plus 2 per tea, and Slip to an adjacent clearing or forest. Daylight actions are paid by exhausting items: Move (boots, plus an extra boot when entering a hostile faction's clearing), Battle (sword; max hits = undamaged swords), Explore (torch: take the ruin item, +1 VP), Aid (any item plus a matching card given to a faction in the clearing; may take an item that faction crafted), Quest (exhaust the 2 items shown), Strike (crossbow: remove one piece), Repair (hammer), Craft (hammers), and a Special action (character-specific, usually costs a torch). Evening: repair everything if in a forest, draw 1 card plus 1 per coin, discard down to 5. Item capacity is 6 plus 2 per bag. Nimble: moves regardless of rule.
factions.how_it_scores: Raising relationships (VP printed on the track); each aid to an Allied faction (2 VP); quests (1 VP per quest of that suit completed so far, or draw 2 cards instead); exploring ruins (1 VP); crafting items; Infamy (an extra VP per piece of a Hostile faction removed in battle). It cannot win by dominance alone and forms a coalition instead (see alternative wins).
factions.board_state_it_creates: Pawn location (clearing or forest); item list with exhausted and damaged states; relationship level with each faction; completed quests by suit; ruins explored. Very readable for 'collect specific items or quest tokens across regions' goals and the best host for item-collection wins.
factions.digital_bot_available: Yes. The built-in AI plays the Vagabond, and the Clockwork 'Vagabot' comes in the Clockwork Expansion DLC.

factions.name: Riverfolk Company
factions.expansion: The Riverfolk Expansion DLC (digital release Apr 28 2021)
factions.engine: Pieces: 15 otter warriors, 9 trade posts (3 per suit). The hand is kept face up. Payments, Funds and Committed boxes hold warriors used as currency. Swimmers: rivers count as paths for them, and they ignore rule when moving along rivers. Services that other players buy with their own warriors: Hand Card, Riverboats (rivers as paths), Mercenaries (rent Riverfolk warriors for rule and battle). A player may buy 1 service, plus 1 more per trade-post clearing where they have pieces; the Riverfolk set prices each Evening. Birdsong: Protectionism (if Payments is empty, add 2), Dividends, and collecting payments into Funds. Daylight: spend or commit funds to Move, Battle, Draw, Recruit, Establish a trade post at a river clearing, or craft by committing funds to the trade-post tracks.
factions.how_it_scores: VP when placing trade posts (printed on the trade-post tracks); Dividends of 1 VP per 2 funds in Birdsong while any trade post is on the map; crafting; removing enemy pieces. Losing a trade post also loses funds.
factions.board_state_it_creates: Trade posts per clearing (all at river clearings), funds count, warriors along the river, which services others bought. Good for 'control the river or trade' goals.
factions.digital_bot_available: Probably, through the built-in AI (unconfirmed per faction). The Clockwork 'Riverfolk Robots' bot is physical Clockwork 2 only, with no evidence of a digital release.

factions.name: Lizard Cult
factions.engine: Pieces: 25 lizard warriors, 15 gardens (5 per suit), an Acolytes box, a Lost Souls pile and an Outcast marker (Outcast or Hated Outcast). Pilgrims: the Cult rules any clearing that has a garden. Lost Souls: cards discarded by other players feed this pile, and its most common suit becomes the Outcast suit. Conspiracies cost acolytes and are done in clearings of the Outcast suit: Crusade (2), Convert (2: an enemy warrior becomes a Lizard), Sanctify (3: an enemy building becomes a garden). Daylight Rituals are paid by revealing cards: Build a garden in a ruled clearing of matching suit, Recruit, Score (sacrifice a card of a suit to score that suit's garden-track value) and Sacrifice (bird card gives an acolyte). Acolytes are gained when Lizard warriors are removed while defending. Gardens are its crafting pieces.
factions.how_it_scores: Mainly the Score ritual: sacrifice a card of a suit to gain VP from that suit's garden track, which pays more the more gardens of that suit are on the map. Also crafting and removing enemy pieces.
factions.board_state_it_creates: Gardens by suit and clearing, warriors, the Outcast suit, acolyte count, the Lost Souls pile. Great for 'convert or spread a doctrine through N clearings' goals.
factions.digital_bot_available: Probably, through the built-in AI (unconfirmed per faction). The Clockwork 'Logical Lizards' bot is physical only.

factions.name: Underground Duchy
factions.expansion: The Underworld Expansion DLC (digital release Mar 30 2023)
factions.engine: Pieces: 20 mole warriors, 3 tunnel tokens, 3 citadels, 3 markets, 9 minister cards (3 squires, 3 nobles, 3 lords) with crowns. The Burrow is an off-map, unsuited clearing the Duchy always rules, adjacent to every clearing with a tunnel; other factions cannot enter it. Birdsong: recruit into the Burrow. Daylight: Assemble actions (Build a citadel or market by revealing matching cards, Recruit, Move, Battle, Dig a tunnel to send warriors out of the Burrow), then Parliament (take the actions of swayed ministers). Evening: Sway a minister by revealing cards that match clearings where the Duchy has pieces (higher rank needs more cards), return revealed cards, craft by activating citadels and markets. Price of Failure: whenever Duchy buildings are removed, the highest-ranked swayed minister returns, its crown is removed permanently, and a random card is discarded.
factions.how_it_scores: Swaying ministers scores VP (higher ranks score more; exact crown values unverified). Also crafting and removing enemy pieces. Lost buildings permanently lose crowns.
factions.board_state_it_creates: Tunnel positions, citadels and markets, warriors in the Burrow versus on the map, swayed ministers (card state). Natural for 'dig out in N regions' or 'emerge from below' goals.
factions.digital_bot_available: Probably, through the built-in AI (unconfirmed per faction). The Clockwork 'Drillbit Duchy' bot is physical only.

factions.name: Corvid Conspiracy
factions.engine: Pieces: 15 crow warriors, 8 plot tokens (2 each of Bomb, Snare, Extortion, Raid) placed face down. Plot: remove warriors to place a face-down plot; each extra plot in the same turn costs more. Trick: swap two plots. Recruit: place a warrior in every clearing of a card's suit. Plus Move and Battle. Flip: reveal a plot in a clearing that has a Corvid warrior. Effects: Bomb removes all enemy pieces, then itself; Snare blocks enemies from placing pieces in or moving out of the clearing; Extortion steals cards; Raid places warriors in adjacent clearings when removed. Embedded Agents: an extra hit when defending with a face-down plot. Exposure: an enemy in the clearing may show a matching card and guess the plot; a correct guess removes it for 1 VP, a wrong guess gives the card to the Corvids. Nimble.
factions.how_it_scores: Each flipped plot scores 1 VP per face-up plot token on the map, then its effect resolves. Also crafting and removing enemy pieces.
factions.board_state_it_creates: Plot tokens (face up or down, type, clearing), warriors spread thin across many clearings. Good for 'secret schemes in N places' or 'reveal schemes' goals.
factions.digital_bot_available: Probably, through the built-in AI (unconfirmed per faction). The Clockwork 'Cogwheel Corvids' bot is physical only.

factions.name: Lord of the Hundreds
factions.expansion: The Marauder Expansion DLC (digital release Jan 14 2025)
factions.engine: Pieces: 20 rat warriors, 1 Warlord pawn, 6 strongholds, 5 mob tokens, 8 Mood cards. The Hoard has a Command track and a Prowess track, filled by items the Hundreds gain; items they cannot store are removed for 1 VP. A mood is chosen each turn and gives an ability, but moods matching hoarded items become unavailable. Command actions (number set by the Command track) are Move, Battle and Build stronghold. Advance: the Warlord moves and battles (number set by Prowess). Mobs are placed by inciting and spread; they destroy enemy buildings and tokens and raid ruins for items. If the Warlord is removed, a warrior is anointed to replace him. The Warlord can loot items in battle (exact rule unverified).
factions.how_it_scores: Oppress in Evening: count clearings they rule that hold a Hundreds piece and no enemy pieces at all: 1-2 clearings = 1 VP, 3-4 = 2, 5 = 3, 6+ = 4 (from search snippet of Law of Root). Plus 1 VP per removed overflow hoard item, removing enemy pieces and crafting.
factions.board_state_it_creates: Strongholds, mob tokens, Warlord location, 'pure' clearings with no enemies, Hoard items. Best host for 'conquer or terrorize N regions' or 'boss' goals.
factions.digital_bot_available: Probably, through the built-in AI (unconfirmed per faction). No Clockwork bot exists for it.

factions.name: Keepers in Iron
factions.engine: Pieces: about 15 badger warriors (count unverified), 3 two-sided waystations (each shows one relic type per side), 12 relic tokens (4 each of figures, tablets, jewelry) with hidden values of 1-3 that start in forests. The Retinue is a set of cards in 3 columns (roughly Move / Battle-then-Delve / Move-or-Recover), resolved like the Eyrie Decree with suit matching; birds are wild. Delve takes a relic from an adjacent forest; Recover is done at a waystation of the relic's type and scores it, but may cost the Retinue card used. Devout Knights: in a clearing with a relic and a Keeper warrior, they ignore the first hit, and each moving warrior can carry one relic. Prized Trophies: an enemy that removes a relic puts it face up in a forest and scores 2 VP total.
factions.how_it_scores: Recovering a relic scores its value (1-3), plus 2 VP for completing a set of the three relic types (exact set rule unverified). Also crafting and removing enemy pieces.
factions.board_state_it_creates: Relics in forests versus clearings (with types), recovered relics by type, waystation positions and faces, warriors. This is the closest native match to 'collect lost things across regions'.
factions.digital_bot_available: Probably, through the built-in AI (unconfirmed per faction). No Clockwork bot exists for it.

factions.name: Homeland factions: Lilypad Diaspora, Twilight Council, Knaves of the Deepwood (NOT in Root Digital)
factions.expansion: Root: The Homeland Expansion, physical only (Leder Games; BGG lists 2026, retail around Aug 2026). No digital release or announcement found as of Oct 2026.
factions.engine: Not usable by a Root Digital mod. Physical flavor only: Lilypad Diaspora are returning exiles; Twilight Council are nocturnal politicians running assemblies; Knaves of the Deepwood play three Vagabond pawns plus skunk meeples and take hostages for ransom. It also adds the Marsh and Gorge maps and a Homeland hireling pack.
factions.how_it_scores: Not applicable to the digital game.
factions.board_state_it_creates: None in the digital game. Do not design rows that depend on these.
factions.digital_bot_available: No, not in the digital game.

vagabond_characters.name: Arbiter

hirelings.name: (General hireling rules as implemented in Root Digital)
hirelings.expansion: Root: Hirelings & Landmarks DLC (Steam app 3874110, released Oct 20 2025, $9.99; Steam and mobile, Switch later)
hirelings.effect: Exactly 3 random hirelings join a game. With 2 players all 3 are Promoted; each player beyond the second turns one into its Demoted form (digital is capped at 4 players, so at most 2 are Demoted). Hirelings start uncontrolled. The first player to reach 4 VP picks a hireling first, then 8 VP and 12 VP pick the next two. On gaining one, the player rolls the control die and places that many control markers; the leader (or anyone tied for the lead) counts only the gold pips, so leaders keep hirelings for less time. At the end of each turn one marker is removed; with none left, the hireling passes to another player. Promoted hirelings have board pieces and a once-per-Daylight action; Demoted ones grant a mostly passive ability. There are 13 pairs: one per digital faction plus 3 neutral.

hirelings.name: Forest Patrol (Promoted) / Feline Physicians (Demoted)
hirelings.expansion: Hirelings & Landmarks DLC (tabletop: Marauder Hirelings Pack). Marquise-aligned.
hirelings.effect: Promoted: cat warriors spread across the map; removed ones return to the card. Once per turn the controller may battle with them or bring all patrol warriors to a clearing that already has one. Demoted: gives the controller the Marquise's Field Hospitals (spend a card to bring removed warriors back).

hirelings.name: Last Dynasty (Promoted) / Bluebird Nobles (Demoted)
hirelings.expansion: Hirelings & Landmarks DLC (tabletop: Marauder Hirelings Pack). Eyrie-aligned.
hirelings.effect: Promoted: the last Eyrie regiment, bird warriors the controller moves and battles with (exact action unverified). Demoted: the controller gains Lords of the Forest (wins ties for rule) and scores VP for clearings ruled (reported as 1 VP per 3; unverified).

hirelings.name: Spring Uprising (Promoted) / Rabbit Scouts (Demoted)
hirelings.expansion: Hirelings & Landmarks DLC (tabletop: Marauder Hirelings Pack). Alliance-aligned.
hirelings.effect: Promoted: uprisings place rabbit warriors in clearings picked by a die roll; the controller influences where they break out or disbands one. Demoted: the controller gets Guerrilla War (as defender, deals hits equal to the higher roll).

hirelings.name: The Exile (Promoted) / The Brigand (Demoted)
hirelings.expansion: Hirelings & Landmarks DLC (tabletop: Marauder Hirelings Pack). Vagabond-aligned.
hirelings.effect: Promoted: a bear pawn that roams the forests (not clearings) as the controller directs and battles enemies in adjacent clearings. Demoted: the Brigand, a stealing ability (exact rule unverified).

hirelings.name: Riverfolk Flotilla (Promoted) / Otter Divers (Demoted)
hirelings.expansion: Hirelings & Landmarks DLC (tabletop: Riverfolk Hirelings Pack). Riverfolk-aligned.
hirelings.effect: Promoted: a boat that travels along the river, gives a card to players at its location, and can move and battle for its controller. Demoted: the controller ignores rule when moving to or from river clearings.

hirelings.name: Warm Sun Prophets (Promoted) / Lizard Envoys (Demoted)
hirelings.expansion: Hirelings & Landmarks DLC (tabletop: Riverfolk Hirelings Pack). Lizard-aligned.
hirelings.effect: Promoted: places lizard warriors that can force enemy movement and battles. Demoted: the controller may search the top 5 cards of the discard pile.

hirelings.name: Sunward Expedition (Promoted) / Mole Artisans (Demoted)
hirelings.expansion: Hirelings & Landmarks DLC (tabletop: Underworld Hirelings Pack). Duchy-aligned.
