landmarks.name: Black Market
landmarks.effect: Lets players exchange a card from hand for one of 3 cards set aside at the landmark, sight unseen. Exact timing and cost unverified.

landmarks.name: Lost City
landmarks.effect: Its clearing counts as fox, rabbit and mouse at once (a wild-suit clearing), so it counts toward any suit check, including dominance.

landmarks.name: Legendary Forge
landmarks.effect: Gives extra benefits when crafting at its clearing ('craft a masterwork'). Exact rule unverified.

landmarks.name: Elder Treetop
landmarks.effect: Goes in a corner clearing and adds an extra building slot there. Removing an enemy building from that clearing scores 1 extra VP.

landmarks.name: Ferry
landmarks.expansion: Native to the Lake map (Underworld DLC). Reported usable on other maps with Hirelings & Landmarks (unverified).
landmarks.effect: Once per turn, pieces moving out of the Ferry's coastal clearing may cross the lake to another coastal clearing; the Ferry moves with them, and the moving player draws 1 card.

landmarks.name: Tower
landmarks.expansion: Native to the Mountain map (Underworld DLC). Reported usable on other maps with Hirelings & Landmarks (unverified).
landmarks.effect: Its clearing becomes 'the Pass'. At the end of a player's Evening, if they rule the Pass, they score 1 VP.

landmarks.name: (Landmark setup rule)
landmarks.effect: The group chooses to play with 1 or 2 landmarks and removes unwanted landmark cards. The rest are shuffled and the chosen number dealt; each card says where its piece goes. In digital this is a game-creation toggle. All 6 landmark cards (Black Market, Lost City, Legendary Forge, Elder Treetop, Ferry, Tower) appear in the tabletop pack.

maps.name: Autumn
maps.features: 12 clearings with fixed printed suits (4 fox, 4 rabbit, 4 mouse), joined by paths, with forests between them. A river runs through several clearings (it matters for Riverfolk, Otter Divers and Flotilla). There are 4 ruins on 'R' slots, each hiding an item. The 4 corner clearings are home sites (Marquise keep and Eyrie roost go in opposite corners; Bird dominance needs two opposite corners). Clearings have 1-3 building slots.

maps.name: Winter
maps.expansion: Free update for Root Digital (no DLC)
maps.features: 12 clearings on a different layout, back side of the Autumn board. Suits are assigned randomly at setup by shuffled suit markers. A 'Raging River' divides the forests the way printed paths do. Ruins sit in different places.

maps.name: Lake
maps.features: 12 clearings around a central lake that acts as a river linking every coastal clearing. The Ferry starts in a coastal corner clearing (see Ferry landmark). Suits are random via suit markers.

maps.name: Mountain
maps.features: 12 clearings. Six closed paths (landslide markers) mean their clearings are not adjacent. Once per turn in Daylight, a player with pieces at either end may spend a card to remove a closed path permanently and score 1 VP. The Tower sits in the central clearing ('the Pass'), worth 1 VP at the end of Evening to whoever rules it. Suits are random.

maps.name: Marsh and Gorge (NOT in digital)
maps.features: No digital release found. Do not design around them.

root.items_and_ruins: Item types: Boots, Bag (satchel/sack), Crossbow, Hammer, Sword, Tea, Coins, and Torch. The Torch belongs only to Vagabonds and cannot be crafted. Craftable items sit in a supply on the map (from memory: 2 boots, 2 bags, 1 crossbow, 1 hammer, 2 swords, 2 teas, 2 coins; not re-verified this session). Crafting an item card takes that item from the supply and scores the VP printed on the card (the Eyrie get only 1). Persistent-effect cards go to the crafter's play area instead. A faction crafts by activating its crafting pieces in clearings whose suits match the card cost: Marquise workshops, Eyrie roosts, Alliance sympathy, Riverfolk funds committed to trade posts, Lizard gardens, and Duchy citadels and markets in Evening. Vagabonds use hammers. Crafted items stay in the faction's crafted-items area, where a Vagabond can take one through Aid and the Hundreds can loot or hoard them. Ruins: 4 ruin chits sit on the 'R' slots of the Autumn map, and each hides a face-down ruin item (bag, boots, hammer, sword, per Law of Root). A ruin fills a building slot until emptied. A Vagabond explores by exhausting a torch, takes the item and scores 1 VP. Lord of the Hundreds mobs can raid ruins for items. The deck has 54 cards (fox, rabbit, mouse and bird suits; birds are wild for costs). It includes 4 dominance cards and 5 ambush cards (one each of fox, rabbit and mouse, plus two bird); ambush cards deal hits when played by a defender. The Exiles & Partisans & Vagabonds DLC adds an alternate 54-card Exiles and Partisans deck with new persistent powers. Mod-readable state: item supply contents, every faction's crafted items, Vagabond item states, ruin contents, Hoard items, and relics (Keepers). Items and relics are the cleanest native objects for 'collect lost things across regions' goals.
root.alternative_wins: Standard win: the first player to reach 30 VP wins immediately. Dominance: four dominance cards exist, one each for fox, rabbit, mouse and bird. In Daylight, a player with at least 10 VP may activate one from hand. Their score marker comes off the track and they can no longer score VP. They win immediately if, at the start of their own Birdsong, they rule 3 clearings of that suit; for Bird dominance, they must rule 2 clearings in opposite corners. A dominance card can also be spent for its suit like a normal card. A discarded dominance card goes face up beside the map instead of the discard pile, and any player may take it by spending a card of matching suit (Law of Root). Coalition: a Vagabond cannot win by dominance. Activating a dominance card instead forms a coalition with the player who has the lowest score, and the Vagabond wins if that partner wins. Digital: dominance and coalitions are implemented, and some built-in Challenges require a dominance win. Mod note: a custom win check can reuse the same pattern (a VP threshold to unlock, a check at the start of Birdsong, a 'rule N clearings of a suit' predicate), which fits how Root already handles a second way to win. 'Rule' means having the most total warriors plus buildings in a clearing. Exceptions: Eyrie win ties, Lizard gardens always rule, and the Duchy always rules the Burrow.
root.digital_edition_modes: Root (Dire Wolf Digital, Unity, Steam app 965580): Steam Early Access Aug 20 2020, full release Sep 24 2020. Also on Mac, iOS, Android and Nintendo Switch. Purchases unlock across platforms through a Dire Wolf account. Maximum 4 players (Dire Wolf said they have no plans for 5-6). Modes: solo against the built-in AI with 3 difficulty levels (exact level names not confirmed); local pass-and-play; online real-time or asynchronous cross-platform multiplayer, with password-protected games and AI to fill empty seats; Challenges (preset scenarios such as dominance-only wins or rivers as paths, more added by each DLC) with achievements; interactive tutorials for every faction; Advanced Setup (draft factions with setup buffs and balanced placement; creating such a game needs 6+ owned factions, but anyone can join one online). DLC and free content: (1) Winter Map, free update. (2) The Clockwork Expansion, about Nov 20 2020: Clockwork bots Mechanical Marquise 2.0, Electric Eyrie, Automated Alliance and Vagabot, presented as a customizable alternative to the normal AI, with 3 difficulty levels plus 1-4 traits each, and co-op play against bots. (3) The Riverfolk Expansion, Apr 28 2021: Riverfolk Company, Lizard Cult, Vagrant, Scoundrel, Arbiter, a second-Vagabond option, 6 challenges, AI improvements. (4) Exiles & Partisans & Vagabonds, May 3 2022, $7.99: the Exiles and Partisans deck plus Adventurer, Ronin and Harrier. (5) The Underworld Expansion, Mar 30 2023: Underground Duchy, Corvid Conspiracy, Lake and Mountain maps, Advanced Setup, challenges. (6) The Marauder Expansion, Jan 14 2025: Lord of the Hundreds, Keepers in Iron, tutorials, challenges and achievements; hirelings were not included at that point. (7) Hirelings & Landmarks, Oct 20 2025, $9.99, Steam app 3874110: 13 hireling pairs and the landmarks, plus 'tighter rules fidelity' and 'smarter opponents' in the same update; Switch version later. NOT found in digital: Clockwork Expansion 2 bots (Logical Lizards, Riverfolk Robots, Cogwheel Corvids, Drillbit Duchy) and the Homeland Expansion (factions or Marsh/Gorge maps). Base-game-only mod versions can rely on Marquise, Eyrie, Alliance, the Vagabond (Thief, Tinker, Ranger), the Autumn and Winter maps, dominance and coalitions, and the standard deck.
uncertainties: Method: WebFetch was egress-blocked for every relevant domain (Dire Wolf news, Steam, steamdb, therootdatabase, root.fandom, ledergames), so all facts come from search-engine snippets plus model knowledge. Treat exact numbers as needing in-game confirmation.

Digital AI coverage: the built-in Dire Wolf AI almost certainly seats every faction you own (AI can fill online seats, and DLC notes mention AI improvements), but no source here confirmed per faction that Lizard, Riverfolk, Duchy, Corvid, Hundreds and Keepers each have an AI. The names of the 3 difficulty levels were not found.

Clockwork bots in digital: only the first Clockwork Expansion (Marquise, Eyrie, Alliance, Vagabot) has evidence of a digital release. The Nintendo store says 3 difficulty levels (the physical game has more). Clockwork Expansion 2 bots show no digital release.

DLC ownership for single-player: unclear whether a player who does not own a DLC can face AI opponents of that DLC's factions offline. For online Advanced Setup, non-owners can join. Assume the creator must own a DLC to use its factions, maps or hirelings.

Hireling effects not confirmed in detail: Last Dynasty, The Exile and The Brigand, Sunward Expedition and Mole Artisans, Raven Sentinels, Flame Bearers and Rat Smugglers, Badger Bodyguards, Furious Protector, Street Band. The Bluebird Nobles VP rate ('1 per 3 clearings') comes from a review snippet. Root Digital uses the newer control-die hireling rules (4/8/12 VP thresholds), not the original 2022 Marauder hireling rules.

Landmarks: exact rules for Black Market (timing, cost) and Legendary Forge (bonus) not confirmed. Reports that Ferry and Tower can be dealt onto any map in digital come from a search summary and are unverified. It is also unconfirmed whether all 6 landmark cards are in the digital deck, though all 6 are in the tabletop pack.

Faction numbers from memory and not re-verified: Marquise building-track and Eyrie roost-track VP values, the Alliance sympathy track, Duchy crown VP per minister rank, the Keepers warrior count and set-completion bonus (snippet says +2 per set of the three relic types), the Corvid Extortion effect, the Scoundrel's Scorched Earth wording, the Hundreds' looting rule, and which pieces the Hundreds, Keepers and Corvids craft with.
Item supply counts (2 boots, 2 bags, 1 crossbow, 1 hammer, 2 swords, 2 teas, 2 coins) and ruin items (bag, boots, hammer, sword) are from memory of Law of Root.

Map suits: whether Root Digital offers a random or balanced suit option on the Autumn map was not confirmed. Winter, Lake and Mountain use random suit markers in the tabletop rules, and digital probably does the same.
Homeland: physical release listed for 2026 (around Aug 2026). No Dire Wolf announcement of a digital Homeland was found as of Oct 2026, so treat it as unavailable.

Engine and modding: Root Digital is Unity, but it is not confirmed whether the Steam PC build is Mono or IL2CPP; that decides BepInEx 5 versus BepInEx 6 IL2CPP or MelonLoader. Check the install folder for GameAssembly.dll (IL2CPP) versus <Game>_Data/Managed/Assembly-CSharp.dll (Mono). Internal class names for board state (clearings, pieces, VP, items) are unknown and must be found by decompiling or with UnityExplorer.
The Oct 2025 Hirelings & Landmarks update promised 'tighter rules fidelity'. Later patches (Root Digital 2.x versions exist) may have changed details listed here.

lore_check.verdict:
The roster is mostly accurate. I could only check through web-search snippets because every wiki fetch was blocked. Nothing is blocking. Four things need fixing before any player-facing text is written: (1) Florrie is in the wrong place; (2) the Paintress's portrait list includes a "painted Alicia" that the lore does not support; (3) Verso is called the lead of Act III, but Act III is Maelle's; (4) spoilers are not handled. Character names, row text and many barks from turn 1 give away the Act III reveals.

Confirmed:
- Combat signatures: Gustave's Overcharge (up to 10 charges in game), Lune's Stains, Sciel's Foretell/Sun/Moon/Twilight, Verso's Perfection D–S, Maelle's stances, Monoco's Bestial Wheel (Agile/Caster/Balanced/Heavy/Almighty) and Nevron feet.
- Monoco is recruited at his Station by beating him in a duel, then the Stalact.
- Rocks: François holds Urrie (relationship level 5 rematch, returning it gives level 6 and diving). Dorrie is in Old Lumière in Act II. Verso gives Esquie Soarrie during the Paintress fight at the Monolith.
- Sciel's husband Pierre and the Aquafarm. Lune's parents were on Expedition 46.
- Clea painted the Nevrons to drain Aline's chroma. The Curator is the real Renoir, trapped under the Monolith. The real Renoir does the erasing; Aline's number is a countdown.
- Act titles are Gustave / Verso / Maelle. Osquio is Esquie's evil cousin. Expedition Flags are real E33 checkpoints, so Gustave's flags are a good fit.

None of the sample barks matched any game dialogue I could find, and the expedition motto is correctly never quoted. The two lore rewrites of the user's ideas hold up: Esquie's "nuts" are really four magic rocks, and the Paintress paints family portraits instead of copying herself. Two new lore facts support the design: as children Clea rode François while Verso rode Esquie (so Clea is the right owner of the François guards), and Esquie once saved Sciel from drowning.

issues.problem: Florrie is placed in Esquie's Nest guarded by 'François' warriors, and lore_basis says 'François the turtle holds Florrie in Act I'. In E33, Esquie claims François stole Florrie. The party beats François, but he hands over a different rock as a trick. The real Florrie is at Stone Wave Cliffs, recovered after the Lampmaster fight at the end of Act I. The fact sheet row for Florrie is also wrong.
issues.fix: Add a 'Stone Wave Cliffs' clearing tag 1–2 steps from the Nest. At setup, spawn Florrie there with 2 guard warriors reskinned as the Lampmaster. Optional Act I joke: a 1-guard François decoy at the Nest. Claiming it gives no rock, plays a 'That's not Florrie!' bark and points to the Cliffs. The bot plan skips the decoy; the Easy bot may fall for it. Keep François as Urrie's holder in Act III, which is correct. Rewrite lore_basis to say 'François fobs the party off with a fake Florrie in Act I and refuses to trade Urrie later; the real Florrie is at Stone Wave Cliffs.'

issues.problem: Her win lets her paint Verso, Clea, Renoir or Alicia, and says Maelle 'IS that painting' / 'Aline's repainting of Alicia' as a fourth family copy. No source shows a painted Alicia. Aline painted copies of Verso, Clea and Renoir. Maelle is the real Alicia, who entered the Canvas at Clea's request and was overwritten by Aline's chroma into a newborn in Lumière.
issues.fix: Use exactly three Portraits, one per suit: Verso, Clea and Renoir. Drop the Alicia option and the Maelle exclusion rule; this also simplifies the bot's site scoring. Correct lore_basis to say 'she painted copies of Verso, Clea and Renoir, and repainted the real Alicia as a newborn (Maelle).'

issues.problem: Character-select names and row text give away Act II/III twists: 'The Curator (the real Renoir Dessendre)', 'Maelle (Alicia Dessendre)', 'Aline Dessendre', the two Renoirs, Verso being a painted copy, Clea existing at all, and Gustave's death (the 'Beach' vignette). Many barks that can fire from turn 1 reveal that the Paintress is Verso's and Maelle's mother: Esquie's 'Mister Verso says his mama...', Sciel's 'somebody's mum', Maelle's 'If she's my mother', the Paintress's 'Your father says...', the Curator's 'Aline. Put the brush down.', Monoco's 'Verso says his mother...' and Verso's 'Mother's been at this table'. The user's own requested gag ('their mother had been playing too many board games') is itself the Act III reveal. The win vignettes for Verso and Maelle also hint at the endings.
issues.fix: Add a spoiler setting on first launch: 'Spoiler-safe' vs 'I've finished E33'. Tag every bark, tooltip and vignette with a tier: safe, Act II, or Act III/ending. In safe mode use neutral display names ('The Curator', 'Maelle', 'The Paintress', 'The White-Haired Man', and Clea shown as '???' until unlocked). Give every 'mother' bark a safe variant, e.g. 'Whoever painted this world has been playing too many board games'. Even with spoilers on, only fire the true 'mother' lines in the mod's Act III. Show ending-flavoured win vignettes only in finished mode.

issues.problem: why_they_matter calls him 'the lead of Act III', which contradicts the Maelle row. The acts are Act I: Gustave, Act II: Verso, Act III: Maelle. The fact sheet's 'Act III, which is titled Verso' is also wrong.
issues.fix: Change the text to 'the lead of Act II, central to Act III and one of the two endings'. Fix the fact sheet too. The campaign framing (Act II = Verso, Act III = Maelle) is already correct.

issues.problem: lore_basis says 'Sciel finds Dorrie in Old Lumière'. The sources only confirm that Dorrie is found in Old Lumière in Act II and given to Esquie after the battle with painted Renoir there, once the party regroups at camp. Who finds it is unconfirmed.
issues.fix: Drop 'Sciel finds it'. Optional lore touch: Dorrie can only be claimed when painted Renoir (Corvid) has no warriors in Old Lumière, echoing that it comes after the Renoir fight.

issues.problem: The rule name 'NEVER MAD' points to Esquie's in-game rhyme ('sad or bad or rad, never mad'). 'Wheee/Whooo' are his signature exclamations.
issues.fix: The two-word rule label and the interjections are fine. Never print the full rhyme or other known Esquie lines in UI text or barks.

issues.problem: 'Lumina Converter' is not verified as the name of his arm. The official replica is sold as the 'Arm of Gustave'. In E33 'Lumina' means the Pictos/Lumina build system (and the Curator's Colour of Lumina), so fans may find the name odd. 'Twin sister Emma' is also unverified; sources only say 'sister'.
issues.fix: Label the gauge 'Gustave's Arm' or 'Overcharge gauge'. Three pips is a fine abstraction of the game's 10 charges. Write 'his sister Emma'.

issues.problem: He is 'never removed' and his Act I death becomes a 'farewell that isn't one'. His death at the end of Act I (painted Renoir's ambush after the Lampmaster, protecting Maelle) is E33's defining twist. Rewriting it is a valid mashup choice, but the vignette both spoils the death and contradicts it.
issues.fix: Present the 'Beach' vignette clearly as a what-if ('This time, the arm held') and put it behind the spoiler setting. Optionally offer a 'Faithful' toggle where Gustave's seat passes to Verso at Act II and keeps his flags.

issues.problem: The Parents' Journal is placed 'in a forest next to the Monolith' with generic justification, and the row says her parents 'raised her to finish their work'. In the lore, her parents were on Expedition 46, which was wiped out near Sirène's Dunes by a Chromatic Glissando. Their bodies and the Expedition 46 journal lie there, and that is her relationship quest.
issues.fix: Tag the Parents' Journal to the forest next to the Sirène-tagged Axon clearing, which is already a Monolith neighbour in the map plan. A 'Glissando' flavour name for any nearby escort fight is optional. Reword to 'her parents left on Expedition 46 and never came back'.

issues.problem: 'Head of the Painters' Council' turned up in no source. Late-game lore also says the real Renoir does the erasing and Aline's number is a countdown or warning. Any text saying she gommages people is wrong after Act II.
issues.fix: Leave the Council title out of player-facing text and rename the Councillor leader to 'The Matriarch'. Make sure tooltips and barks say she paints the number, never that she erases people.

issues.problem: 'His protégé Noco' is unverified; sources call Noco a friendly Gestral merchant whom Monoco's final quest brings back at the Sacred River in Act III, with a Golgra fight there. 'With Esquie, he rescues Verso and Alicia' is also unconfirmed. Barks like 'Monoco would like them' have him speak in the third person. No source shows that, and he is described as oddly scholarly and polite yet bloodthirsty.
issues.fix: Write 'his friend Noco'. Drop or verify the rescue claim. Rewrite the barks in first person in his polite-brawler voice, e.g. 'I would like your feet. Respectfully.' The same check applies to Esquie's third-person line ('Esquie is much too round').

issues.problem: The row says he was 'imprisoned beneath the Monolith by Aline'. Sources say he has been trapped beneath the Monolith since the Fracture caused by his clash with Aline, and acts through the faceless Curator form.
issues.fix: Reword to 'trapped beneath the Monolith since the Fracture'. Everything else in the row checks out: he helps the expedition, his power does the Gommage, and he is the final boss in Lumière.

issues.problem: 'Regent of the Flying Manor' is unverified, and the row blends the real Clea and her painted copy without explaining the split. Sources say the real Clea entered the Canvas, captured Aline's gentle painted Clea and repainted her into a Nevron-producing tool, and that Clea painted the Nevrons to drain Aline's chroma.
issues.fix: Drop 'Regent'. Frame the seat as the real Clea working through her captured copy in the Flying Manor. Add a lore line that backs her as Esquie's guard host: as children Verso rode Esquie and Clea rode François.

issues.problem: The 'dark Nevrons' and the 'Noirs Rising' plot name are not confirmed. Sources show the white-haired man massacring the expedition himself on landing. The bark 'Thirty-three of you this year' also treats the expedition's number as its headcount.
issues.fix: Call the warriors 'Renoir's Nevrons' and note it as design liberty. Rename the Raid plot to something like 'Ambush on the Shore'. Rewrite the bark as 'Expedition Thirty-Three. Next year, Thirty-Two. That's arithmetic, not cruelty.' His Expedition Zero tie is confirmed: Verso calls him his former commander.

issues.problem: She rides the Thief, and Steal is reskinned as 'quick fingers'. Nothing in E33 makes Maelle a thief; she is a fencer.
issues.fix: Reskin Steal as a fencer's 'Disarm' (a feint that takes a card). Use the Ronin's Swift Strike as her riposte when Exiles & Partisans is owned.

issues.problem: The facts check out: Pierre, the Aquafarm, Sophie as her best friend, and the lost child. But the bark 'Pierre always wanted a bigger farm...' jokes about her dead husband. Her backstory includes Pierre's fatal accident, a suicide attempt in the sea, and losing their unborn child, so the joke may read as flippant.
issues.fix: Replace it with a warm line that isn't a joke (e.g. about the school or the Aquafarm). An optional spoiler-gated Act III pair: Esquie and Sciel trade a gentle bark, since Esquie is the one who pulled her out of the sea.

issues.problem: The win can become impossible on the default v1 table. A Portrait identity (Verso, Clea, Renoir, Alicia) is used up when a roost is placed, and with Maelle seated only 3 exist. Eyrie Build cards stay in the Decree until Turmoil, so the Decree keeps forcing roosts into the same suit, and each of those uses up an identity. On Gustave + Paintress + Sciel + Maelle she can end up with all 3 identities on only 2 suits. The only way to get one back is for an enemy to destroy a roost, and her bot cannot destroy its own. The Maelle exclusion is also inconsistent with the lore. The seated Verso, painted Renoir and painted Clea are also her paintings. Applying the same logic to them would leave her unable to win at a full E33 table.
issues.fix: Don't store Portraits; work them out at check time. A Portrait is any Living roost outside the Monolith, and she needs one Living roost in each of fox, rabbit and mouse. Identity is cosmetic and is reassigned at each check (a seated family member's portrait reads 'as she remembers them'). Drop the Maelle exclusion. This also survives save/load because there is no event-written PortraitMap.

issues.problem: He effectively cannot win on the v1 base table, where the Paintress is always seated. Vagabond max hits equal his undamaged swords, and the Ranger starts with 1. The Monolith is the Eyrie home: a roost plus the 3+ warriors her bot_plan keeps there. A defender deals the lower die, so the chance of taking no damage in a battle against warriors is 7/16. Even with 2 swords and the +1 from rank A/S, clearing 2 warriors and a roost with no damage is about 25% per attempt. After that, any faction can void the Birdsong check just by moving one warrior or pawn into the Monolith, and the spoiler layer on every bot will always do that.
issues.fix: Base the confirmation on Perfection, not on the Monolith staying empty. Announce at end of turn if he is rank S, in the Monolith, and removed the last enemy warrior there this turn (no enemy buildings left). He wins at his next Birdsong if he is still in the Monolith at rank S. Pieces that only walk in do not void it. To stop him, someone must battle him and land a hit, which drops him off S. That matches the lore that any hit breaks his rank. For Easy, allow rank A plus 2 undamaged swords.

issues.problem: The guard spawns have three problems. (a) Root most likely stores warriors as per-faction counts per clearing, so guards cannot be told apart from the host's own warriors. The Marquise already has a setup warrior in the Nest and marches more in. 'guardSeat has 0 warriors' then means clearing every host warrior there, and 'host never moves guards' needs a filter on the host's moves. (b) 2-3 free warriors from supply give the host rule of the Nest (Gustave can build and flag it). (c) In v1, Clea needs Riverfolk, so the host is the Marquise or Eyrie. Under native rules, removing their warriors makes that faction Hostile, and Esquie then pays an extra boot to enter clearings with its warriors. Marquise warriors are in 11 of 12 clearings at setup, so his movement is crippled. That also breaks Never Mad, and the bot's 'Aid a friend to attack the guards' step makes no sense when the friend is the host.
issues.fix: Track guardsLeft per rock as a mod counter set to the spawned count, and decrement it when the host loses warriors in that clearing in any battle. The rock becomes loose at 0, and the host's own extra warriors do not matter. Enforce 'guards stay' as a count floor in the host's move generator for that clearing. The host may not build, recruit or place in a clearing with a guarded rock. Move Friends Not Foes into v1: one prefix patch skips the hostility change for warriors removed in a guarded-rock clearing. Host priority: Clea, then the non-Marquise faction with the most warriors in supply, then the Marquise. Remove the host from the bot's Aid-a-friend step. If placing another seat's warriors is not possible, make the no-spawn fallback the v1 default.

issues.problem: The win is close to automatic. Marquise setup puts a warrior in every clearing except the Monolith, so he rules its neighbours from turn 1. He builds 1-3 times a turn, and because flags are permanent, the Lumière-to-Beachhead chain finishes in Act I and can never be cut. The Route bot is therefore cosmetic. The charge fills from battles where he only defends, so bots attacking him charge it for him. Act II starts when anyone reaches 10 VP, often Gustave himself, so the check can fire on his first Act II turn (around round 3-4), far ahead of the 30 VP pace. The only answer is flipping rule of one Beachhead. The Beach vignette's +1 charge is also a scripted edge, which contradicts the rule that 'act events are vignettes only'.
issues.fix: Bring back the ruled supply line: at both checks he must currently rule every clearing of some flagged chain from Lumière to the Beachhead. Flags stay as visual legacy and route memory. Charge goes +1 only for a battle he starts that removes at least one enemy piece. The Beachhead must hold a Marquise building at both checks. Optionally require flagged clearings in all 3 suits. Make the Beach vignette cosmetic. Opponents can then answer anywhere along the route.

issues.problem: He wins too easily, and nobody gets a turn to answer. The Warlord Advances and battles every turn. Heavy, Caster, Agile and Balanced are routine within 4-6 rounds, because wood, sympathy and roosts are everywhere. Almighty is 'any piece of the leader who isn't Monoco', which he gets the turn after Act III opens. Quest wins fire instantly with no VP gate, so the Monoco bot will usually win around round 8 and be the strongest bot at the table. Naming clash: the Hoard is renamed 'Trophy Wheel', and so is the feet tracker.
issues.fix: Add a 10 VP gate. Feet must come from at least 3 different factions (or every opponent if fewer). Almighty means removing a building of the current VP leader, or winning one battle in which Hundreds remove 3+ of the leader's pieces. If the Warlord dies, he loses his most recent foot and Almighty. Alternatively, make it an area-style win: announce at 5 feet, and he wins at his next Birdsong if the Warlord is still on the map. Rename the Hoard 'Gestral Stash' and keep 'Bestial Wheel' for the feet.

issues.problem: The win is too fragile at confirmation. A Sanctuary breaks the moment any warrior, pawn, building or token enters. Between her announce and her Birdsong, any bot with a warrior next door voids it with one move (paying an Outrage card), and the Vagabond can wander in for free. The spoiler layer on every bot makes an exact 5-Sanctuary win almost unreachable. In v1, Gustave also starts with warriors in 11 clearings, which her 10 warriors must evict first.
issues.fix: Announce on strict Sanctuaries as written. Confirm at Birdsong on Lanterns still standing in 5+ clearings across 3 suits, with no enemy building or token in them, and at least 1 base standing. Enemy warriors or pawns that only walked in (and paid Outrage) do not void it. To stop her, you must remove a Lantern or raze a base, which is the Alliance's real counterplay. Optionally require 6 Sanctuaries at the announce.

issues.problem: Same fragility, and it is hard to set up as well. Any single warrior or Vagabond pawn stepping into one ring clearing voids the check. Snares stop placing pieces and moving out, not moving in. Ring clearings start with Marquise setup warriors, and the Corvids (15 warriors, weak in battle) must clear them and then keep every intruder out for a full round against spoiler bots. Like Verso and Sciel, this is an 'emptiness' test that one move answers.
issues.fix: Base it on rule instead. Every ring clearing holds a Renoir piece (warrior or plot) and is ruled by no faction other than Renoir or the Paintress, and the Monolith itself holds no other Vagabond pawn. Use the same test at the announce and at Birdsong. A face-up Snare in a ring clearing counts as his hold there even if he is outnumbered. Opponents must then win battles or out-stack him to stop it.

issues.problem: The bot_plan assumes a move action the Lizard Cult does not have. Lizards have no normal Move. Their only movement is the Crusade conspiracy (2 acolytes, starting from an Outcast-suit clearing), so 'split single warriors into adjacent clearings' cannot be built. Also, counting the Esquie guard stacks she hosts gives her a covered clearing for free.
issues.fix: Rewrite the bot plan. Spread through the Recruit ritual (it places a warrior by the revealed card's suit; confirm the exact wording against Law of Root) and through Convert in Outcast-suit clearings. Save bird cards for the Monolith. Use Crusade only for the Monolith push when the Monolith or its neighbour is the Outcast suit. Don't count guard warriors toward her 8-clearing total.

issues.problem: The setup tunnel in the Monolith makes the Burrow adjacent to the Eyrie home from turn 1. Duchy warriors can pour into the Paintress's home in Act I; the bot holds back, but a human Curator won't. It also uses 2 of the Duchy's 3 tunnels (home plus Monolith), leaving 1 to reach Lumière. If Gustave isn't seated, Lumière can be an empty corner, and the Curator can dig in and rule it the moment Act III starts.
issues.fix: Make the Monolith tunnel a mod overlay called 'Cell Crack'. It does not connect to the Burrow and does not count against his tunnels until Act III, when it becomes a real tunnel from his supply, or a free one if all three are on the map. That matches the lore: he is imprisoned until the reveal. When Lumière is not someone's home clearing, also require a Duchy building there, or rule with 3+ warriors.

issues.problem: The whole bot design assumes Root's AI exposes lists of candidate moves that the mod can re-score. Nothing confirms this. The Dire Wolf AI may produce whole-turn plans or run an internal search, and whether the build is IL2CPP or Mono changes how practical Harmony patching is. If re-ranking isn't possible, every bot_plan falls apart.
issues.fix: Spend week 1 on a spike: decompile and find each faction's AI decision entry points. Make the main path a mod-owned priority policy that asks the engine for legal options through the same API the human UI uses to highlight clickable clearings, cards and items, and submits actions. Hand only the remaining sub-decisions (hit allocation, ambush, discards) to the native AI. The bot_plans are already priority lists in the style of the Clockwork flowcharts, so they port directly with no new search AI.

issues.problem: Clockwork bots (Mechanical Marquise 2.0, Electric Eyrie, Automated Alliance, Vagabot) play simplified rules: different economies, decrees and item handling. Checks and Goal Director hooks written against standard faction state (Supporters, wood, the relationship track, Decree resolvability) would misread or crash.
issues.fix: In E33 mode, every seat uses the standard Dire Wolf AI and the Clockwork options are hidden. Say this explicitly in each needs_dlc/engine note.

issues.problem: Overcharge ('may spend'), Stains ('may spend') and Belly Bounce (choosing the Bag as a sword) each need a new choice prompt inside Root's battle flow. That is new mid-battle UI, plus a new AI decision for each.
issues.fix: v1: Belly Bounce applies automatically, with the Bag counting as 1 sword in a rock clearing and no prompt. Overcharge and Stains become pre-battle toggles on the faction-board overlay, outside the battle flow. The bot sets them by its priority rule, e.g. Overcharge only when it takes the Beachhead or saves Lumière. Sciel's Twilight and Verso's Perfection are already automatic.

issues.problem: Activating a dominance card removes the player's VP marker, so 'VP>=10' is undefined. It is also unspecified whether a Vagabond in a coalition can still chase its own themed win (Esquie's has no VP gate), or whether it wins when its partner wins thematically.
issues.fix: State that themed wins are off while a player has an active dominance card or is in a coalition. A coalition Vagabond wins if its partner wins in any way, as in standard Root.

issues.problem: Some state comes from events (charge, rank, feet, rock status, act clock). It is lost or goes wrong on save/load, a resumed game, or any in-engine undo or rollback, which makes win checks unreliable.
issues.fix: Derive state from the board wherever possible: Portraits, Sanctuaries, ring, coverage and Beachhead rule. Save the rest alongside the game, keyed to its ID, and re-check it against the board on load.

issues.problem: The win text has no Act gate, but how_checked uses act>=2. The Keepers usually have all 3 relic types by round 4-5, so the win comes down to one tagged relic. A value-3 tablet may not exist in every relic mix.
issues.fix: Put the Act II gate in the win text. Place (or reveal) the Parents' Journal in its forest only at the start of Act II, like Dorrie. Tag the highest-value tablet instead of 'value 3'.

issues.problem: In v1 there is only one Vagabond seat, so Verso is never seated alongside him. Soarrie therefore always sits loose in the Monolith, and he just walks in and takes it: a free rock.
issues.fix: When Verso isn't seated, the Monolith's ruler holds Soarrie. Esquie claims it by Aiding that faction once while in the Monolith, or freely once no one rules the Monolith.

issues.problem: Alicia Awakens (+1 relationship with the Paintress) and the Beach (+1 Gustave charge) are scripted edges, which contradicts 'act events are vignettes only'. The relationship bump's VP and its cap are unspecified. In 2-player games Maelle needs only 1 Allied faction, which is easy.
issues.fix: The bump gives no track VP and can't go past Friendly; alternatively make both cosmetic. In 2-player games require Allied with the one faction plus 15 VP.

issues.character: Roster similarity (Sciel / Clea / Renoir / Verso; Esquie / Lune)
issues.problem: As written, four wins are presence or emptiness counts, and all are beaten the same way: move one piece in. Esquie and Lune both fetch tagged objects from near the Nest or Monolith.
issues.fix: The Birdsong fixes above separate them: Sciel becomes Lantern survival, Verso no-hit, Renoir rule of the ring, and Clea stays raw coverage. Keep Esquie as guarded fights and Lune as convoys, with the Journal revealed only in Act II, so the two play differently.

build_check.verdict: The overall pattern works: each character rides an existing Root faction, adds a win checked from board or mod state at end of turn or at Birdsong, and gets a priority-list bot. The DLC tags are correct: Riverfolk for Clea and a second Vagabond, Marauder for Lune and Monoco, Underworld for the Curator, painted Renoir and the Lake/Mountain maps, and Exiles & Partisans & Vagabonds for the Ronin. No row depends on Homeland. Two rows are blocking. First, the Paintress's portrait names are used up when a roost is placed, so with Maelle seated she can end up unable to win; work Portraits out at check time and drop the exclusion. Second, Verso's 'Monolith empty at Birdsong' is effectively unwinnable against a seated Eyrie and spoiler bots; confirm on rank S instead. Sciel and Renoir have the same weakness, because one piece walking in breaks the win; confirm on Lanterns still standing and on rule. Gustave (permanent flags and passive charge) and Monoco (instant quest win with an easy Almighty foot) are too easy. Esquie's guard spawns need count-based tracking and the no-hostility patch in v1. Clea's bot plan uses a Move the Lizards don't have. The Curator's setup tunnel gives Burrow access to the Monolith on turn 1. The main technical risk: the Goal Director assumes Root's AI can be re-scored. Prove that with a decompile spike, and plan for a mod-owned priority bot that drives the engine's legal-action API. With these fixes, the v1 base-game set (Gustave, Paintress, Sciel, plus one of Esquie, Verso or Maelle) can be built and won by human and bot alike, and the bots stay beatable. Maelle and the Paintress (after her fix) are the closest to ready.
